196: static int gc9d01_push(FAR struct gc9d01_fb_s *priv)
197: {
198:   clock_t start = clock_systime_ticks();
199: 
200:   if (priv->fbmem == NULL || priv->bus < 0)
201:     {
202:       return -ENODEV;
203:     }
204: 
205:   if (!bk7258_gc9d01_window_full(priv->display))
206:     {
207:       return -EIO;
208:     }
209: 
210:   if (!bk7258_lcd_spi_write_frame(priv->bus, priv->fbmem, GC9D01_FBLEN))
211:     {
212:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: pixel burst failed\n", priv->display);
213:       return -EIO;
214:     }
215: 
216:   priv->updates++;
217: 
218:   {
219:     uint32_t ms = TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - start);
220: 
221:     priv->report_updates++;
222:     priv->report_ms += ms;
223:     if (ms > priv->report_max_ms)
224:       {
225:         priv->report_max_ms = ms;
226:       }
227: 
228:     /* Report a rolling bus cost without logging every frame.  This makes it
229:      * possible to distinguish LVGL scheduling delay from LCD transfer time
230:      * during a long-press test. */
231:     if ((priv->updates % 32u) == 0)
232:       {
233:         printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: 32 updates avg=%ums max=%ums total=%u\n",
234:                priv->display,
235:                (unsigned int)(priv->report_ms / priv->report_updates),
236:                (unsigned int)priv->report_max_ms,
237:                (unsigned int)priv->updates);
238:         priv->report_updates = 0;
239:         priv->report_ms = 0;
240:         priv->report_max_ms = 0;
241:       }
242:   }
243: 
244:   /* First few pushes get a timing report: it is the only way to know the
245:    * real cost of a frame on this bus, which decides whether the preview
246:    * path needs DMA.  After that stay quiet -- this runs per displayed
247:    * frame.
248:    */
249: 
250:   if (priv->updates <= 3)
251:     {
252:       uint32_t ms = TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - start);
253: 
254:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: update %u: %d bytes in %ums "
255:              "(%u frames on bus)\n", priv->display,
256:              (unsigned int)priv->updates, GC9D01_FBLEN, (unsigned int)ms,
257:              (unsigned int)bk7258_lcd_spi_frame_count(priv->bus));
258:     }
259: 
260:   return OK;
261: }

578: bool bk7258_lcd_spi_write_frame(int bus, const void *frame, size_t len)
579: {
580:   FAR struct lcd_bus_s *b = lcd_bus(bus);
581:   const uint32_t *src = frame;
582:   size_t words = len / 4u;
583:   size_t i;
584: 
585:   if (b == NULL || !b->initialized || frame == NULL || len == 0 ||
586:       (len & 3u) != 0)
587:     {
588:       return false;
589:     }
590: 
591:   /* RAMWR goes out as an ordinary DC-low command; CS is allowed to
592:    * deassert afterwards, exactly as bk_lcd_spi_frame_display() does.
593:    */
594: 
595:   if (!bk7258_lcd_spi_write_cmd(bus, GC9D01_CMD_RAMWR))
596:     {
597:       return false;
598:     }
599: 
600:   bk7258_gpio_write(b->dc_pin, true);
601: 
602:   /* lcd_spi_quad_write_start(): park the command channel, hold CS low for
603:    * the whole burst, hand the data line to the memory-mapped window and
604:    * stop the command path from generating SCK.
605:    */
606: 
607:   putreg32(0, b->base + QSPI_OFF_CMD_C_L);
608:   putreg32(0, b->base + QSPI_OFF_CMD_C_H);
609:   putreg32(0, b->base + QSPI_OFF_CMD_C_CFG1);
610:   putreg32(0, b->base + QSPI_OFF_CMD_C_CFG2);
611: 
612:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, 0, QSPI_CONFIG_FORCE_SPI_CS_LOW);
613:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, 0, QSPI_CONFIG_IO_CPU_MEM_SEL);
614:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, 0, QSPI_CONFIG_DISABLE_CMD_SCK);
615: 
616:   if (b->frames < 2)
617:     {
618:       printf("bk7258_lcd_spi[%s]: frame %u: config=0x%08x words=%u "
619:              "src=%p first_px=0x%04x swap=%u\n", b->name,
620:              (unsigned int)b->frames,
621:              (unsigned int)getreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG),
622:              (unsigned int)words, frame,
623:               (unsigned int)(src[0] & 0xffff),
624:              (unsigned int)g_swap_bytes);
625:     }
626: 
627:   /* CPU-driven copy.  The controller back-pressures the AHB write when its
628:    * FIFO is full, so this self-throttles to the wire rate; 160x160 RGB565
629:    * measured ~27ms on the bus.
630:    *
631:    * The destination address increments: lcd_spi_dma_single_mode_config()
632:    * sets dst.start_addr = qspi_data, dst.end_addr = qspi_data + data_len
633:    * and dst.addr_inc_en = DMA_ADDR_INC_ENABLE, so the window is a range,
634:    * not a single FIFO register.
635:    */
636: 
637:   if (g_swap_bytes)
638:     {
639:       for (i = 0; i < words; i++)
640:         {
641:           putreg32(gc9_swap16x2(src[i]), b->window + i * 4u);
642:         }
643:     }
644:   else
645:     {
646:       for (i = 0; i < words; i++)
647:         {
648:           putreg32(src[i], b->window + i * 4u);
649:         }
650:     }
651: 
652:   up_udelay(QSPI_FRAME_TAIL_DELAY_US);
653: 
654:   /* lcd_spi_quad_write_stop(), same order as the reference. */
655: 
656:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, QSPI_CONFIG_DISABLE_CMD_SCK, 0);
657:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, QSPI_CONFIG_FORCE_SPI_CS_LOW, 0);
658:   modifyreg32(b->base + QSPI_OFF_CONFIG, QSPI_CONFIG_IO_CPU_MEM_SEL, 0);
659: 
660:   b->frames++;
661:   return true;
662: }

当前剩余延迟不是单一原因。按影响程度看，主要有以下几项。

**1. 当前代码主动跳过了 PRESS 刷新**

这是“按下按键后没有立即反馈”的最直接原因。

[vs_app.c:1349](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_app.c:1349) 只有非 `VS_INPUT_PRESS` 事件才触发渲染：

```c
if (event.type != VS_INPUT_PRESS)
  {
    render_input = true;
  }
```

因此当前时序是：

```text
按下
-> 产生 PRESS
-> 只修改 runtime，不刷新屏幕
-> 等待用户松手
-> 产生 SHORT
-> 执行翻页
-> 刷新屏幕
```

短按操作本身又是在释放时才确认，[vs_input.c:118](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_input.c:118)：

```c
else if (!state->long_sent &&
         now - state->pressed_ms >= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MIN_MS &&
         now - state->pressed_ms <= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS)
  {
    event->type = VS_INPUT_SHORT;
  }
```

所以从“手指开始按下”到真正动作，必然包含用户按住时间。之前日志中的短按时间为：

```text
96~204 ms
```

即使屏幕链路完全无延迟，页面动作也只能在松手后的 `100~200 ms` 左右开始。

同样，长按动画在前 `500 ms` 完全不会产生进度事件：

```c
if (held <= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS)
  continue;
```

因此长按动画固定存在：

```text
前 500 ms：无进度
后 1500 ms：0% -> 100%
```

如果用户以按下时刻作为动画开始时刻，首先就会感觉有半秒延迟。

**2. 相同 style 和 flag 仍然被重复设置，导致大量无意义重绘**

上一轮只优化了相同文字：

```c
if (strcmp(lv_label_get_text(label), value) != 0)
  lv_label_set_text(label, value);
```

但状态屏每次更新仍会给三个按键重复设置：

[vs_display.c:283](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_display.c:283)

```c
lv_obj_set_style_text_color(...);
lv_obj_set_style_bg_color(...);
lv_obj_set_style_bg_opa(...);
```

状态主文字每次也重复设置颜色：

```c
lv_obj_set_style_text_color(panel->body, ...);
```

这些 LVGL style setter 没有“新值等于旧值就退出”的保护。最终都会进入：

[lv_obj_style.c:356](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/core/lv_obj_style.c:356)

```c
lv_style_set_prop(style, prop, value);
lv_obj_refresh_style(obj, selector, prop);
```

而 `lv_obj_refresh_style()` 最终无条件执行：

```c
lv_obj_invalidate(obj);
```

因此即使颜色完全没有变化，每个状态更新仍会：

```text
刷新 style cache
-> invalidate 对象
-> LVGL 重新绘制
```

更严重的是进度对象：

[vs_display.c:240](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/velasight/vs_display.c:240)

```c
if (visible)
  {
    lv_obj_remove_flag(panel->progress, LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN);
    lv_arc_set_value(panel->progress, snapshot->progress);
  }
else
  {
    lv_obj_add_flag(panel->progress, LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN);
  }
```

LVGL 的 `lv_obj_add_flag()` 和 `lv_obj_remove_flag()` 对 `HIDDEN` 没有先检查当前状态，重复调用也会 invalidate：

[lv_obj.c:117](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/apps/graphics/lvgl/lvgl/src/core/lv_obj.c:117)

```c
if (f & LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN)
  lv_obj_invalidate(obj);
```

所以当前仍存在：

```text
相同文字不重绘
但相同颜色、背景、可见状态仍反复触发重绘
```

这很可能是字体优化后收益有限的主要软件原因。

**3. 长按进度环本身接近满屏，而且走复杂软件绘制**

进度环尺寸为：

```c
lv_obj_set_size(panel->progress, 152, 152);
```

屏幕只有：

```text
160 × 160
```

也就是说进度环的包围框占：

```text
152 × 152 = 23104 pixels
整屏       = 25600 pixels
占比       ≈ 90.25%
```

即使实现 dirty-area 刷新，进度环变化也可能让约 90% 的屏幕区域变脏。

此外 `lv_arc` 不是简单矩形填充。它涉及：

```text
角度计算
圆弧 mask
抗锯齿
前景/背景混合
```

当前还开启了：

```text
CONFIG_LV_DRAW_SW_COMPLEX=y
```

而 framebuffer 位于 `kmm_zalloc()` 分配的内部 SRAM：

[bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c:293](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c:293)

```c

- UI 线程被占用
- LVGL 不能处理下一帧
- 页面动作不能继续
- CPU 不能并行准备下一帧

DMA不是约半秒首帧延迟的唯一原因，但在字库优化后，它已经成为更显著的动画瓶颈。尤其进度环接近满屏，局部刷新收益有限时，DMA或提高单帧传输效率会更重要。

**综合延迟模型**

当前短按从物理按下到页面可见，大致是：

```text
用户按住时间              100~200 ms
GPIO 去抖和 UI 轮询          5~15 ms
LVGL 两屏软件重绘          未测，可能几十到数百 ms
状态屏整帧传输              24~26 ms
内容屏整帧传输              24~26 ms
主循环 sleep                  5 ms
```

长按动画每帧大致是：

```text
大圆弧复杂软件绘制
+ 非缓存 framebuffer 写入
+ 24~26 ms CPU PIO 整帧传输
+ 5 ms 主循环 sleep
```

并且长按开始前固定等待 `500 ms`。

**优先级判断**

目前最值得优先处理的是：

1. 恢复 PRESS 的轻量即时反馈，但不要通过完整 `vs_render_status()` 重绘整屏。
2. 给 style、hidden flag 和颜色 setter 增加状态比较，只修改真正变化的对象。
3. 不再用 `page` 字段无条件将两块屏幕都标脏，完全按屏幕实际 snapshot 字段判断。
4. 缩小进度环，或改成更便宜的线性/分段点阵进度指示。
5. 实现按键区域的局部 LCD 更新。
6. 最后再做 DMA或双控制器并行传输。

其中第 1 条主要解决“按下后没有立即响应”，第 2、3 条主要解决单击页面切换，第 2、4、6 条主要决定长按动画帧率。当前字体已不再是首要瓶颈。

410: int vs_display_render(struct vs_display_s *display,
411:                       const struct vs_ui_snapshot_s *snapshot)
412: {
413:   bool content_dirty;
414:   bool status_dirty;
415: 
416:   if (display == NULL || snapshot == NULL)
417:     return -EINVAL;
418: 
419:   /* fb1 is the physical left content display; fb0 is the physical right
420:    * status display. */
421:   content_dirty = !display->previous_valid ||
422:                   vs_content_changed(snapshot, &display->previous);
423:   status_dirty = !display->previous_valid ||
424:                  vs_status_changed(snapshot, &display->previous);
425:   if (content_dirty)
426:     vs_render_content(&display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL], snapshot);
427:   if (status_dirty)
428:     vs_render_status(&display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL], snapshot);
429: 
430:   if (!display->revealed)
431:     {
432:       /* Match the old synchronous boot animation's hand-off: both complete
433:        * frames must reach panel GRAM before the shared backlight is enabled.
434:        * lv_refr_now() executes each framebuffer's FBIO_UPDATE synchronously. */
435: 
436:       lv_obj_invalidate(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].screen);
437:       lv_obj_invalidate(display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL].screen);
438:       lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].display);
439:       lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL].display);
440: #ifdef CONFIG_LVX_USE_DEMO_CONTEST2026_264_VELASIGHT
441:       bk7258_display_reveal();
442: #endif
443:       display->revealed = true;
444:     }
445:   else
446:     {
447:       /* State changes normally wait for LVGL's 33 ms refresh timer.  That
448:        * timer is too coarse for button feedback, and a full-frame LCD push
449:        * can make the next timer pass arrive even later.  Flush only the
450:        * panels changed by this snapshot now; the regular timer remains
451:        * responsible for its own animations such as the waiting suffix. */
452:       if (status_dirty)
453:         lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].display);
454:       if (content_dirty)
455:         lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL].display);
456:     }
457:   display->previous = *snapshot;
458:   display->previous_valid = true;
459:   display->waiting = snapshot->progress_kind == VS_PROGRESS_WAIT;
460:   snprintf(display->wait_meta, sizeof(display->wait_meta), "%s",
461:            snapshot->status_meta);
462:   if (!display->waiting)
463:     {
464:       display->wait_phase = 0;
465:       display->wait_next_ms = 0;
466:     }
467:   return 0;
468: }

470: void vs_display_tick(struct vs_display_s *display)
471: {
472:   if (display != NULL)
473:     {
474:       uint32_t now = vs_display_now_ms();
475: 
476:       if (display->waiting &&
477:           (display->wait_next_ms == 0 ||
478:            (int32_t)(now - display->wait_next_ms) >= 0))
479:         {
480:           static const char *const phases[] = {".", "..", "...", ""};
481:           char meta[VS_TEXT_LONG];
482: 
483:           snprintf(meta, sizeof(meta), "%s%s", display->wait_meta,
484:                    phases[display->wait_phase]);
485:           vs_set_label(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].meta,
486:                        meta);
487:           display->wait_phase = (display->wait_phase + 1) % 4;
488:           display->wait_next_ms = now + 350;
489:         }
490:       lv_timer_handler();
491:     }
492: }

12: 		A TCP service the development machine's browser talks to through
13: 		host/console.py: read and write kvdb, configure Wi-Fi, start apps,
14: 		stream the syslog, stream JPEG frames from /dev/video0.
15: 
16: 		It replaces the "type a serial command, then run b64frames.py on
17: 		the transcript" loop.  Nothing about HTTP lives on the board: the
18: 		page and the WebSocket are the development machine's job, so the
19: 		page can be edited and reloaded without reflashing.
20: 
21: 		Access control is the kvdb key 'web.allow' -- one IPv4 address or
22: 		CIDR block, or several separated by commas.  With that key unset
23: 		the service does not listen at all, so the first setup has to go
24: 		through the serial console once.  A permissive default would make
25: 		the whitelist decoration and would allow the state where someone
26: 		believes it is in force while the board is open to the subnet.

Author: [REDACTED-USER] <[REDACTED-INTERNAL-EMAIL]>
Date:   Mon Aug 10 20:20:11 2026 +0800

    feat(audio): add BK7258 internal-DAC playback and capture
    
    Bring up the chip's built-in analog audio block on the AP core: mono
    playback through the internal DAC and capture from the analog microphone
    front end, exposed as /dev/audio/pcm0p and /dev/audio/pcm0c.
    
    Hardware path, from the board schematic:
    
      internal DAC -> AUDLP/AUDLN differential (pins 24/25) -> C48
                   -> HT6872 class-D amplifier (U8) -> CN8 speaker
      GPIO50 (net PA_SD) -> R70 1K -> HT6872 CTRL, R71 10K pulls it low so the
                   amplifier is muted at power-on
    
      CN7 electret microphone -> MIC1 -> analog ADC
    
    An I2S codec is not an option here: the board has none, and both of
    BK7258's selectable I2S1 pin groups are already taken -- GPIO9 by the
    vibration motor's PWM3 output and GPIO42/43 by the camera's control bus.
    
    Implementation notes:
    
    - AUD_CLK_CONTROL bit0|bit1 must stay set, not be pulsed.  The vendor
      header names bit0 ADC_SOFT_RESET, which reads like a pulse; implementing
      it that way holds the ADC in reset and it returns no samples at all.
      Exhaustive measurement over the four combinations: 0 and 2 give zero
      samples, 1 gives 4760 (26 percent dropped), 3 gives exactly 6400 for a
      200 ms window at 16 kHz.
    
    - Analog register writes go through an SPI-like indirect path and must poll
      the busy bit (bit number equals the register number) or writes are lost.
    
    - The AUDP power domain and the AUD module clock are requested from CP1 over
      the PWC mailbox channel, so audio bring-up has to run in
      board_late_initialize() after bk7258_pwc_start(), like the camera.  The
      two PWC votes cannot be sent back to back: the mailbox channel allows one
      in-flight message, so each vote waits for its reply.
    
    - Transfers are interrupt-driven FIFO rather than DMA.  bk7258_dma.c is a
      single fixed channel with no channel selection, and 16 kHz mono runs with
      zero underruns without it.
    
    - Capture is mono.  MIC2 is wired as a hardware echo reference on the
      schematic, but it reads exactly zero: the chip has one ADC and MIC2 has no
      bias.  A MIC2-only probe saturates (RMS ~32530 against a 32767 full
      scale), confirming there is no second data path.  The AEC reference is
      left to software; CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_AEC_REFERENCE keeps the interleaved
      two-channel layout available if that ever changes.
    
    - Only 8/16/32 kHz are supported.  Those come off the XTAL path; 44.1 and
      48 kHz need APLL, which is not ported, so aud_clk_config() rejects it
      rather than guessing at the calibration registers.
    
    The audio_test command exercises the driver: play (sine), rec (per-channel
    DC, RMS and peak), loop (live passthrough), recplay (record into RAM then
    play it back) and diag (register dump).  It reports numbers instead of
    writing files because the AP mounts only procfs and the console is a
    mailbox command-injection path, so there is nowhere to put a WAV file and
    no way to pull one back out.  The first 8 captured buffers are discarded:
    the analog front end has not settled and including them reported peak
    32767 against an RMS of 1100 in a quiet room.

new file mode 100755

--- /dev/null
+++ b/build_and_flash.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)
+CONTEST_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd -P)
+SDK_ROOT="$CONTEST_ROOT/bk_avdk_smp"
+OPENVELA_ROOT="$CONTEST_ROOT/contest"
+AP_CONFIG="vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent"
+AP_OUT="$OPENVELA_ROOT/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent"
+PACKAGE="$SDK_ROOT/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin"
+AP_BIN="$AP_OUT/nuttx.bin"
+AP_INPUT="$SDK_ROOT/build/openvela-ap.bin"
+AP_PACKED="$SDK_ROOT/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/tmp/app1.bin"
+LOG_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/logs/runtime"
+
+PORT=${VELASIGHT_PORT:-/dev/ttyUSB0}
+PORT_NUM=${VELASIGHT_PORT_NUM:-}
+FLASH_BAUD=${VELASIGHT_FLASH_BAUD:-1500000}
+CONSOLE_BAUD=${VELASIGHT_CONSOLE_BAUD:-115200}
+BOOT_LOG_SECONDS=${VELASIGHT_BOOT_LOG_SECONDS:-25}
+DO_FLASH=0
+
+die()
+{
+  printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+usage()
+{
+  printf '%s\n' \
+    'usage: build_and_flash.sh [--flash] [-p port] [-n loader-port]' \
+    '       [--boot-log-seconds seconds]' \
+    'Builds ai_agent, regenerates the 4148K-aligned AP layout, packages all-app.bin,' \
+    'and optionally flashes it with the shell-based autoflash workflow.'
+}
+
+while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --flash) DO_FLASH=1 ;;
+    -p) shift; PORT=$1 ;;
+    -n) shift; PORT_NUM=$1 ;;
+    --boot-log-seconds) shift; BOOT_LOG_SECONDS=$1 ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+
+command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'podman is required'
+command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'sha256sum is required'
+command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'cmp is required'
+
+cd "$OPENVELA_ROOT"
+./build.sh "$AP_CONFIG" --cmake distclean
+./build.sh "$AP_CONFIG" --cmake -j8
+
+test -s "$AP_BIN" || die "missing AP binary: $AP_BIN"
+grep -q '^CONFIG_LV_TXT_ENC_UTF8=y$' "$AP_OUT/.config" || die 'UTF-8 is disabled'
+grep -q '^CONFIG_LV_FONT_FMT_TXT_LARGE=y$' "$AP_OUT/.config" || die 'large LVGL font format is disabled'
+grep -q '^CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS=500$' "$AP_OUT/.config" || die 'short-press limit is not 500 ms'
+grep -q 'velasight_font_16_ui' "$AP_OUT/System.map" || die 'UI font is not linked'
+grep -q -- '--range 0x4e00-0x9fff' "$SCRIPT_DIR/app/velasight/velasight_font_16_ui.c" || die 'full CJK font range is missing'
+grep -q 'voice_vad_process' "$AP_OUT/System.map" || die 'VAD is not linked'
+grep -q 'velaclaw_client_open' "$AP_OUT/System.map" || die 'local ai_agent client is not linked'
+
+AP_SIZE=$(stat -c%s -- "$AP_BIN")
+AP_LIMIT=$((3904 * 1024))
+[ "$AP_SIZE" -le "$AP_LIMIT" ] || die "AP binary exceeds 3904K raw linker region: $AP_SIZE > $AP_LIMIT"
+
+mkdir -p "$(dirname -- "$AP_INPUT")"
+cp -- "$AP_BIN" "$AP_INPUT"
+
+cd "$SDK_ROOT"
+make -C projects/app_ab clean
+podman run --rm --userns=keep-id \
+  -v "$SDK_ROOT:/armino" \
+  -w /armino \
+  localhost/bekencorp/armino-idk:1.5 \
+  make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 \
+  SDK_DIR=/armino \
+  EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin
+
+PARTITIONS="$SDK_ROOT/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/partitions/partitions.txt"
+test -s "$PACKAGE" || die 'all-app.bin is missing'
+test -s "$AP_PACKED" || die 'packed AP input is missing'
+grep -q 'primary_ap_app.*4148K' "$PARTITIONS" || die 'AP partition is not 4148K'
+cmp -s "$AP_BIN" "$AP_INPUT" || die 'external AP copy differs'
+cmp -s "$AP_BIN" "$AP_PACKED" || die 'packed AP input differs'
+
+IMAGE_SIZE=$(stat -c%s -- "$PACKAGE")
+IMAGE_SHA=$(sha256sum -- "$PACKAGE" | cut -d' ' -f1)
+
+if [ "$DO_FLASH" -eq 1 ]; then
+  cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"
+  FLASH_ARGS=(-b "$FLASH_BAUD" -B "$CONSOLE_BAUD" -p "$PORT")
+  if [ -n "$PORT_NUM" ]; then
+    FLASH_ARGS+=(-n "$PORT_NUM")
+  fi
+  AUTOFLASH_EXPECTED_SIZE="$IMAGE_SIZE" \
+    ./autoflash.sh "${FLASH_ARGS[@]}"
+
+  mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+  BOOT_LOG="$LOG_DIR/velasight-final-boot-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
+  stty -F "$PORT" "$CONSOLE_BAUD" cs8 -cstopb -parenb raw -echo -crtscts
+  timeout --foreground "$BOOT_LOG_SECONDS" tee "$BOOT_LOG" < "$PORT" >/dev/null &
+  CAPTURE_PID=$!
+  sleep 0.5
+  printf '\035' > "$PORT"
+  sleep 0.05
+  printf '.' > "$PORT"
+  sleep 0.05
+  printf '\r\n' > "$PORT"
+  sleep 0.05
+  printf 'reboot\r\n' > "$PORT"
+  wait "$CAPTURE_PID" || true
+  printf 'boot log: %s\n' "$BOOT_LOG"
+  tr '\r' '\n' < "$BOOT_LOG" | tee "${BOOT_LOG%.log}.normalized.log"
+fi

3: What this board needs in order to run `packages/ai_agent`, and which parts of
4: that belong here rather than upstream.
5: 
6: Build config: `../configs/ai_agent/defconfig`. This is a product configuration,
7: not the minimal `nsh` baseline. `nsh` is retained for AP bring-up and comparison;
8: `ai_agent` adds the Wi-Fi/IPv4 dependencies, mbedTLS, cJSON, the agent itself,
9: VelaSight and its LVGL display configuration. Building `nsh` instead produces a
10: valid minimal AP image but cannot validate or display the VelaSight product UI.
11: 
12: Two things `nsh` has and this config deliberately does not: the V4L2 M2M JPEG
13: codec (`CONFIG_BK7258_JPEG_ENC`, `/dev/video1`) and on-device libjpeg
14: (`CONFIG_LIB_JPEG_TURBO`), and with them the `jpeg_test` command, whose Kconfig
15: `depends on BK7258_JPEG_ENC`. **The camera's JPEG path does not need any of
16: them** -- capture-side encoding lives in the chip-level
17: `board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_jpeg_enc.c`, which is compiled
18: unconditionally, and `bk7258_jpeg_enc_write_header` is present in this config's
19: `System.map`. `jpeg_test` and the M2M codec exist to exercise the encoder as a
20: standalone transcoder; the agent has no use for that, so the config leaves them
21: out rather than spending flash on them.
22: 
23: ```sh
24: cd <openvela work tree root>
25: sh contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/ai_agent/apply.sh
26: ./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent --cmake -j8
27: ```
28: 
29: `-Werror` cannot be used with this config: `packages/ai_agent` itself does not
30: build warning-free (see "Upstream defects" below). The `nsh` config keeps
31: `-Werror`.
32: 
33: ## Measured footprint
34: 
35: From the linker's own report (`-Wl,--print-memory-usage`), both configs
36: rebuilt clean at commit `422bef0`, with all six `app/` linkfiles in place (as
37: a fresh `repo sync` produces them):
38: 
39: | Region | `nsh` | `ai_agent` | Region size |
40: |---|---|---|---|
41: | FLASH | 485184 B (43.55%) | 691008 B (62.02%) | 1088 KB (`FLASH` 0x110000) |
42: | RAM | 122160 B (35.51%) | 186112 B (54.09%) | 336 KB (`RAM` 0x54000) |
43: | PSRAM_SECTION | 0 B | 0 B | 6 MB |
44: 
45: `ai_agent` leaves 413 KB of flash spare in the historical no-LVGL measurement.
46: The gap to `nsh` is 201 KB, but it is
47: not a clean "cost of the agent": this config adds mbedTLS, cJSON, the agent and
48: `agent_camera`, and drops `jpeg_test`. The Wi-Fi driver and the IPv4 stack are
49: in both, which is why the gap is much smaller than the 371 KB this file used to
50: record.
51: 
52: Two things make these numbers easy to get wrong, both worth checking before
53: quoting them: whether the `app/` linkfiles are present (a missing one silently
54: removes that app, `docs/reference/platform.md` §6), and whether the build
55: directory was wiped after a defconfig change.
56: 
57: RAM here is the static footprint only, and it is the interesting half: those
58: 186 KB leave the SRAM heap with a 158 KB arena, which is *not* enough to
59: start the agent. See "`ai_agent` itself" below.
60: 
61: ## Camera path
62: 
63: `camera_capture` (`src/tools/tool_camera.c`) is the only agent tool that
64: touches this board's camera. It opens `/dev/video0`, sets a compressed
65: format, uses two `V4L2_MEMORY_MMAP` buffers, waits with `poll()` and hands
66: the frame to a Vision LLM.
67: 
68: What already matches:
69: 
70: - **MMAP buffers land in PSRAM.** `v4l2_cap.c` calls
71:   `imgdata_ops_s.alloc()` when one exists, and this board's implementation
72:   takes the buffer from `PSRAM_POOL_DISPLAY` (`bk7258_camera_imgdata.c`).
73:   That is what makes a 160 KB × 2 buffer heap possible on a board whose AP
74:   kernel heap is smaller than that, and it is also required: YUV_BUF can
75:   only write into `0x60000000..0x61000000` (invariant 5 in
76:   `docs/reference/camera.md`).
77: - **`sizeimage` decides the buffer size.** For a compressed format
78:   `get_bufsize()` returns `sizeimage` rather than `width*height`, so the
79:   tool's 160 KB hint is what gets allocated per buffer.
80: - **The same MMAP + `poll` + `DQBUF` shape is already proven on this board**

3:  *
4:  * Continuous capture split into fixed-length chunks and uploaded while the
5:  * next chunk is still being recorded.
6:  *
7:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

10: #ifndef __APP_AUDIO_TEST_AUDIO_TEST_STREAM_H

12: 
13: /****************************************************************************
14:  * Included Files
15:  ****************************************************************************/
16: 
17: #include <nuttx/config.h>
18: 
19: #include <stddef.h>
20: #include <stdint.h>
21: 
22: /****************************************************************************
23:  * Public Types
24:  ****************************************************************************/
25: 
26: /* Opaque: everything in here is shared between the capture thread and the
27:  * uploader, and the locking that makes that safe is this module's business
28:  * alone.
29:  */
30: 
31: struct audio_test_stream_ctx_s;
32: 
33: /****************************************************************************
34:  * Public Function Prototypes
35:  ****************************************************************************/
36: 
37: /****************************************************************************
38:  * Name: audio_test_stream_open
39:  *
40:  * Description:
41:  *   Allocate the chunk ring and start the uploader thread.
42:  *
43:  *   The ring is what decouples the two halves.  Capture runs on a deadline
44:  *   it does not control -- the ADC delivers a buffer every few milliseconds
45:  *   whether or not anyone is ready for it -- while an upload takes as long
46:  *   as the network feels like taking.  Handing a chunk straight to a socket
47:  *   from the capture path would make every network stall a capture stall,
48:  *   and the plan is explicit that congestion must not block audio, the
49:  *   mailbox heartbeat or the keys.  So capture only ever copies into a free
50:  *   slot and signals; if the uploader has fallen behind, capture discards
51:  *   the oldest queued chunk and keeps recording rather than waiting for it.
52:  *
53:  *   Dropping a chunk is a deliberate choice and not a silent one: the
54:  *   upload protocol tolerates a gap in the sequence numbers, and a counted
55:  *   drop reported at the end is far better than audio that stutters
56:  *   whenever Wi-Fi does.
57:  *
58:  * Input Parameters:
59:  *   host     - IPv4 address of the receiver, in dotted-quad form
60:  *   port     - TCP port it is listening on
61:  *   rate     - sample rate of the audio that will be fed in
62:  *   chunk_ms - chunk length in milliseconds
63:  *   bitrate  - Opus target bits per second
64:  *
65:  * Returned Value:
66:  *   A context, or NULL on failure (a message has been printed).
67:  *
68:  ****************************************************************************/
69: 
70: struct audio_test_stream_ctx_s *
71: audio_test_stream_open(const char *host, int port, unsigned int rate,
72:                        unsigned int chunk_ms, unsigned int bitrate);
73: 
74: /****************************************************************************
75:  * Name: audio_test_stream_feed
76:  *
77:  * Description:
78:  *   Hand captured samples to the chunker.  Called from the capture thread
79:  *   once per buffer the driver returns.
80:  *
81:  *   Never blocks and never fails: if there is nowhere to put the samples it
82:  *   frees a slot by dropping the oldest chunk that has not started
83:  *   uploading yet.
84:  *
85:  * Input Parameters:
86:  *   ctx      - from audio_test_stream_open()
87:  *   samples  - interleaved 16-bit samples as they came from the driver
88:  *   nsamples - number of samples available at samples, all channels
89:  *   stride   - 1 for mono, 2 to take the left channel of an interleaved
90:  *              pair.  With the AEC echo reference compiled in the capture
91:  *              stream is L/R interleaved and only the left channel is the
92:  *              microphone, so the de-interleave happens here rather than
93:  *              forcing the caller to stage a copy of every buffer.
94:  *
95:  ****************************************************************************/
96: 
97: void audio_test_stream_feed(struct audio_test_stream_ctx_s *ctx,
98:                             const int16_t *samples, size_t nsamples,
99:                             unsigned int stride);
100: 
101: /****************************************************************************
102:  * Name: audio_test_stream_close
103:  *
104:  * Description:
105:  *   Flush whatever is queued, stop the uploader and release everything.
106:  *
107:  *   A partially filled chunk is sent too: the last couple of seconds of a
108:  *   session are usually the reason it was started.
109:  *
110:  ****************************************************************************/
111: 
112: void audio_test_stream_close(struct audio_test_stream_ctx_s *ctx);
113: 
114: /****************************************************************************
115:  * Name: audio_test_stream_report
116:  *
117:  * Description:
118:  *   Print the running counters.  Safe to call while capture is running.
119:  *
120:  ****************************************************************************/
121: 
122: void audio_test_stream_report(struct audio_test_stream_ctx_s *ctx);
123: 
124: #endif /* __APP_AUDIO_TEST_AUDIO_TEST_STREAM_H */

1: #!/bin/sh
2: ############################################################################
3: # board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/ai_agent/apply.sh
4: #
5: # Applies this board's ai_agent patches to packages/ai_agent in the openvela
6: # work tree.  Idempotent: a patch that already reverse-applies is skipped.
7: #
8: # These changes belong upstream, not here.  They live in this repository only
9: # so the board can be built and flashed before the pull request against
10: # open-vela/packages_ai_agent (branch dev-ai-contest-2026) is merged; see
11: # README.md in this directory for what each patch does and why.
12: #
13: # Usage (from anywhere):
14: #   sh board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/ai_agent/apply.sh [--revert]
15: #
16: # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
17: ############################################################################
18: 
19: set -e
20: 
21: here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
22: 
23: # The openvela work tree root is this repository's parent directory: the repo
24: # manifest checks this repository out as a subdirectory of it.  From here that
25: # is seven levels up (ai_agent, bk7258-ap, bk7258, boards, beken, board, repo).
26: 
27: root=$(cd "$here/../../../../../../.." && pwd)
28: target="$root/packages/ai_agent"
29: 
30: if [ ! -d "$target/.git" ]; then
31:   echo "apply.sh: $target is not a git checkout" >&2
32:   exit 1
33: fi
34: 
35: revert=no
36: if [ "$1" = "--revert" ]; then
37:   revert=yes
38: fi
39: 
40: for patch in "$here"/[0-9]*.patch; do
41:   [ -e "$patch" ] || continue
42:   name=$(basename "$patch")
43: 
44:   if [ "$revert" = yes ]; then
45:     if git -C "$target" apply --reverse --check "$patch" 2>/dev/null; then
46:       git -C "$target" apply --reverse "$patch"
47:       echo "apply.sh: reverted $name"
48:     else
49:       echo "apply.sh: $name not applied, nothing to revert"
50:     fi
51:     continue
52:   fi
53: 
54:   if git -C "$target" apply --reverse --check "$patch" 2>/dev/null; then
55:     echo "apply.sh: $name already applied"
56:   elif git -C "$target" apply --check "$patch" 2>/dev/null; then
57:     git -C "$target" apply "$patch"
58:     echo "apply.sh: applied $name"
59:   else
60:     echo "apply.sh: $name does not apply cleanly -- upstream moved?" >&2
61:     exit 1
62:   fi
63: done

1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: set -euo pipefail
3: 
4: SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
5: WORK_DIR=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/velasight-font
6: FONT_VERSION=17.0.05
7: FONT_FILE="$WORK_DIR/unifont-$FONT_VERSION.otf"
8: FONT_URL="https://unifoundry.com/pub/unifont/unifont-$FONT_VERSION/font-builds/unifont-$FONT_VERSION.otf"
9: FONT_SHA256=85701ab9b1e251ee16f4df00b13f22eac311d72b7dab427a7d975fe7f5064702
10: CHARSET_BIN="$WORK_DIR/gb2312-level1.bin"
11: CHARSET_UTF8="$WORK_DIR/gb2312-level1.txt"
12: OUTPUT="$SCRIPT_DIR/velasight_font_16_ui.c"
13: 
14: mkdir -p "$WORK_DIR"
15: if [ ! -f "$FONT_FILE" ]; then
16:   curl --fail --location --output "$FONT_FILE" "$FONT_URL"
17: fi
18: printf '%s  %s\n' "$FONT_SHA256" "$FONT_FILE" | sha256sum --check --status
19: 
20: # GB2312 rows B0-D7 are the 3,755 level-one Chinese characters.
21: node - "$CHARSET_BIN" <<'NODE'
22: const fs = require('fs');
23: const output = process.argv[2];
24: const bytes = [];
25: for (let row = 0xb0; row <= 0xd7; row++) {
26:   for (let column = 0xa1; column <= 0xfe; column++) {
27:     bytes.push(row, column);
28:   }
29: }
30: fs.writeFileSync(output, Buffer.from(bytes));
31: NODE
32: iconv -c -f GB2312 -t UTF-8 -o "$CHARSET_UTF8" "$CHARSET_BIN"
33: CHAR_COUNT=$(wc -m < "$CHARSET_UTF8")
34: [ "$CHAR_COUNT" -eq 3755 ] || {
35:   printf 'unexpected GB2312 level-one character count: %s\n' "$CHAR_COUNT" >&2
36:   exit 1
37: }
38: 
39: npx --yes lv_font_conv@1.5.3 \
40:   --font "$FONT_FILE" \
41:   --size 16 \
42:   --bpp 1 \
43:   --no-prefilter \
44:   --no-kerning \
45:   --range 0x20-0x7f \
46:   --symbols "$(tr -d '\n' < "$CHARSET_UTF8")聆" \
47:   --format lvgl \
48:   --output "$OUTPUT" \
49:   --lv-font-name velasight_font_16_ui \
50:   --force-fast-kern-format
51: 
52: # Keep generated metadata reviewable and independent of temporary paths.
53: node - "$OUTPUT" <<'NODE'
54: const fs = require('fs');
55: const path = process.argv[2];
56: let source = fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
57: source = source.replace(
58:   /^ \* Opts:.*$/m,
59:   ' * Source: GNU Unifont 17.0.05; ASCII + GB2312 level-one 3755 + U+8046; --bpp 1 --no-prefilter --no-kerning'
60: );
61: fs.writeFileSync(path, source.trimEnd() + '\n');
62: NODE

text:
**原因**
1. `vs_acknowledge()` 在之前的非阻塞改造中只设置高亮状态，不再立即调用 `vs_render()`。
2. 输入事件按批处理。如果 `PRESS` 和 `SHORT` 在同一批次被取出，批末只渲染一次，此时页面动作已经完成，原页面的高亮帧从未显示。
3. 默认的 `VS_PAGE_HISTORY_BLANK` 照片问答页没有配置确认软键，显示层还显式隐藏该页的确认键，因此该页面按确认键始终无法显示高亮。

**修复**
- `vs_acknowledge()` 设置响应状态后立即调用 `vs_render()`，确保高亮帧先送到屏幕。
- 没有恢复旧的 `usleep(120000)`，UI 线程仍然是非阻塞的。
- 为照片问答首页恢复确认软键文字“拍照提问”。
- 移除显示层对照片问答页确认软键的强制隐藏。

1: ---
2: name: autoflash
3: description: "Flash a BK7258 board without pressing RST by hand. Use when: 烧录 BK7258, flash BK7258, autoflash, all-app.bin, bk_loader, Getting Bus, Gotten Bus, 手动按 RST, 免按复位, 自动烧录, 串口被占用, Device or resource busy, screen is terminating, 烧完打字没反应, 烧录进度条, 烧录卡住, 烧录超时, 波特率 1500000, dev/ttyUSB0."
4: ---
5: 
6: # autoflash — BK7258 免按 RST 自动烧录
7: 
8: `bk_loader` 只能靠拨 DTR/RTS 来复位板子，而这块板**没有自动复位电路**，所以原始流程需要人在 `Getting Bus...` 循环期间手按 RST。
9: 
10: `autoflash.sh` 用软件复位替代按键：在 `bk_loader` 握手循环期间，从另一个进程往同一个串口写 `reboot`，让还在运行的固件自己复位，正好撞上 bootrom 的监听窗口。
11: 
12: ## 快速开始
13: 
14: ```bash
15: sg dialout -c "./autoflash.sh -a"                 # 烧默认镜像，烧完自动挂串口
16: sg dialout -c "./autoflash.sh -b 1500000 -a"      # 高速烧录，40 秒而不是 4 分钟
17: sg dialout -c "./autoflash.sh -t"                 # 只测握手，不写 flash
18: ```
19: 
20: 需要 `sg dialout`（串口属 dialout 组）。
21: 
22: ## 第一次用：先改一行
23: 
24: 脚本顶部有一行工作区根目录，**换机器必须改**：
25: 
26: ```bash
27: # ############################################################################
28: # 改这一行：你的工作区根目录（里面应有 tools/ 和 bk_avdk_smp/）
29: # ############################################################################
30: ROOT=/home/mi/vela_competition_ap_console_dev
31: ```
32: 
33: 它派生出两个路径 —— `$ROOT/tools/bk_loader`（烧录器）和 `$ROOT/bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin`（默认镜像）。
34: 
35: 不想改文件就用环境变量：
36: 
37: ```bash
38: VELA_WS=/your/workspace ./autoflash.sh -a
39: ```
40: 
41: ROOT 不对时报错会带上当前值和该改哪里，不会只丢一句"文件不存在"。
42: 
43: ## 参数
44: 
45: | 参数 | 含义 |
46: |---|---|
47: `-i <file>` | 要烧的镜像，默认 `bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin` |
48: `-p <port>` | 串口设备，默认 `/dev/ttyUSB0` |
49: `-n <num>` | `bk_loader` 的端口号，默认 `0` |
50: `-b <baud>` | **烧录**波特率，默认 `115200`。只影响下载速度 |
51: `-B <baud>` | **控制台**波特率，默认 `115200`。固件编译期定死，一般别动 |
52: `-s` | 跳过 `all-app.bin` 字节数校验 |
53: `-a` | 烧完自动挂 `screen` 看日志 |
54: `-t` | 只测握手，用 `read` 代替 `download`，不碰 flash |
55: `-h` | 显示帮助 |
56: 
57: 环境变量 `VELA_WS=/path/to/workspace` 可覆盖脚本里写的 `ROOT`。
58: 
59: ## 它替你做的五件事
60: 
61: 1. **释放串口** — 自动关掉 detached 的 `screen` 会话和残留 `cat`。这是最高频的失败原因
62: 2. **烧前校验** — 打印 SHA256；当前 `2992K` AP 分区产品包必须为
63:    `4,526,080` 字节，打包不完整直接拒绝。分区变化后用
64:    `AUTOFLASH_EXPECTED_SIZE` 更新校验值。
65: 3. **软复位** — 最多 8 次，每次先发 AP 控制台逃逸序列再发 `reboot`
66: 4. **实时进度条** — 擦除和写入两条进度条照常滚动
67: 5. **恢复串口速率** — 高速烧录后把串口拨回控制台波特率
68: 
69: ## 波特率：两个独立的概念
70: 
71: **这是最容易搞错的地方。** `-b` 和控制台速率是两件事：
72: 
73: - `-b 1500000` 只让 `bk_loader` 传得快，2.6 MB 从 4 分钟降到 40 秒
74: - 固件控制台**始终**是 defconfig 里定死的 115200
75: 
76: 把 `-b` 的值用在烧完后的 `screen` 上，你会看到乱码且打字无反应。脚本内部严格分开这两个变量，并在结束时把串口拨回控制台速率。
77: 
78: CH340 的上限是 2 Mbps —— `stty` 会直接拒绝 `6000000`，那个数字只是 `bk_loader` 的参数范围。
79: 
80: ## 前置条件
81: 
82: | 条件 | 检查 |
83: |---|---|
84: 串口存在 | `ls /dev/ttyUSB*` |
85: 在 dialout 组 | `id \| grep dialout`，不在就 `sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER` 然后**重新登录** |
86: 镜像已打包 | 脚本**不编译**。改了代码要先走编译 + 打包两步 |
87: 固件还活着 | 软复位依赖固件能响应 `reboot`。固件崩死时仍需手按 RST |
88: 
89: ## 常见问题
90: 
91: **提示要手动按 RST** — 软复位 8 次没拿到总线。按一次 RST 然后**彻底松手**，`bk_loader` 循环还在跑，按下去就接上。连按会在 `Gotten Bus`/`Getting Bus` 之间反复跳，永远进不了擦除。
92: 
93: **`Device or resource busy`** — 有进程占着串口。脚本会自动清，清不掉会明确报出占用者 PID。手动查：
94: 
95: ```bash
96: screen -ls                                    # 有没有 detached 会话
97: sg dialout -c "fuser -v /dev/ttyUSB0" 2>&1    # 表格输出走 stderr，必须 2>&1
98: ```
99: 
100: `lsof` 在非 root 下查不出串口占用，别用它下判断。
101: 
102: **`screen` 一开就 `[screen is terminating]`** — 有 detached 会话攥着串口。`Ctrl-A D` 是**分离**，会话继续占串口；要释放必须 `Ctrl-A K` 再按 `y`。
103: 
104: **烧完打字没反应** — 串口还停在烧录波特率。拨回来：
105: 
106: ```bash
107: sg dialout -c "stty -F /dev/ttyUSB0 115200 cs8 -cstopb -parenb raw -echo -crtscts"
108: ```
109: 
110: **烧到中途被掐断** — flash 已擦除但只写了一部分，板子起不来，且此时固件不响应 `reboot`。必须手按 RST 重烧一次完整的。脚本的超时按镜像大小自动计算（传输时间 ×2 + 60 秒），不会再出现这种情况。
111: 
112: ## 为什么这样能行（关键实测事实）
113: 
114: 写这个脚本时踩过的坑，都是靠实测而非推理定下来的：
115: 
116: **DTR/RTS 没接复位电路** — 分别脉冲两条线，各收到 0 字节。`bk_loader` 里确实有 `SetDTR`/`ClearRTS`/`do_reset_signal`，但在这块板上无效。
117: 
118: **bootrom 窗口约 473 ms** — 发 `reboot` 后 0.005s→0.478s 是静默期，1.04 s 就进 `nsh>`。窗口够宽。
119: 
120: **`bk_loader` 始终在 115200 握手** — 即使传 `-b 1500000`，日志也报 `BaudRate : 115200`，握手成功后才升速。所以循环期间写 `reboot` 总是有效的，与 `-b` 无关。
121: 
122: **`bk_loader` 不独占 tty** — 没设 `TIOCEXCL`，所以第二个进程能往同一端口写。
123: 
124: **转义序列后必须加换行** — CP shell 按行解析。`\x1d` `.` `reboot\r\n` 三次分开写但中间没换行，会被拼成 `.reboot` 这个不存在的命令，板子根本不重启。加 `\r\n` 把那行冲掉才行。
125: 
126: **拿到总线后立刻停止写入** — 每 100 ms 轮询日志里的 `Gotten Bus`，一出现就停。之后再往端口写任何字节都会破坏下载协议。
127: 
128: ## 完整流程（改了代码之后）
129: 
130: 脚本只烧不编译，所以完整链条是三步：
131: 
132: ```bash
133: # 1. 编译 AP 核。nsh 仅是最小对照配置；VelaSight 产品必须使用 ai_agent。
134: cd <workspace>/contest
135: export PATH=$PWD/prebuilts/gcc/linux-x86_64/arm-none-eabi/bin:$PATH
136: ./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent --cmake -j8
137: 
138: # 2. 打包
139: cd <workspace>
140: cp contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/nuttx.bin bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
141: cd bk_avdk_smp
142: sg docker -c "./dbuild.sh make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 SDK_DIR=/armino EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin"
143: 
144: # 3. 烧录
145: sg dialout -c "<repo>/.claude/skills/autoflash/autoflash.sh -b 1500000 -a"
146: ```
147: 
148: 打包后建议核对三处，确认烧的是刚编的：
149: 
150: ```bash
151: cmp contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/nuttx.bin bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
152: cmp contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/nuttx.bin bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/tmp/app1.bin
153: stat -c%s bk_avdk_smp/projects/app_ab/build/bk7258/app_ab/package/all-app.bin   # 当前必须 4526080
154: ```
155: 
156: ## 板上两个 shell
157: 
158: 串口上挂着两个 shell，提示符不同：
159: 
160: | 提示符 | 是谁 |
161: |---|---|
162: `$` | CP 核（armino），串口的直接归属者 |
163: `nsh>` | AP 核（OpenVela），经 mailbox 桥接 |
164: 
165: ```
166: $ ap_console open          进入 AP 控制台
167: Ctrl-] 松手再按 .           退回 CP shell
168: ```
169: 
170: `reboot` **必须发给 CP shell**，AP 那边不管重启 —— 这也是脚本发 `reboot` 前先发逃逸序列的原因。`ap_cmd` 在真板上不工作（`bridge tx=0`），要用 `ap_console open` 透传。

98: static uint16_t ring_count(uint16_t read_index, uint16_t write_index,
99:                            uint16_t size)
100: {
101:   return write_index >= read_index ? write_index - read_index :
102:          size - read_index + write_index;
103: }

105: static uint16_t tx_count(void)
106: {
107:   return ring_count(g_uart.tx_read, g_uart.tx_write, MB_UART_TX_SIZE);

125: static void update_local_rts(void)
126: {
127:   bool new_rts = g_uart.upper_rts || rx_free() <= MB_UART_RTS_ASSERT;

129:   if (new_rts != g_uart.local_rts)
130:     {

132:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
133:       if (new_rts)
134:         {
135:           g_uart.stats.rts_assert++;
136:         }
137:       else

144: static bool valid_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack)
145: {
146:   return ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & ~3u) == 0 &&
147:          ack->payload_length == 0 && ack->flags == 0 && ack->crc8 == 0 &&
148:          ack->reserved == 0;
149: }

151: static void mb_uart_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
152:                                 int result, void *arg)
153: {
154:   uint8_t command;
155:   bool failed;
156: 
157:   (void)arg;
158:   /* The mailbox transport invokes completion callbacks with interrupts
159:    * disabled, so this callback updates UART state directly.
160:    */
161:   command = ack == NULL ? g_uart.transaction_command :
162:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(ack);
163:   failed = result < 0 || !valid_ack(ack) ||
164:            (ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & 2u) != 0);
165: 
166:   if (ack != NULL && valid_ack(ack))
167:     {
168:       g_uart.peer_rts = (ack->payload_address & 1u) != 0;
169:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
170:     }
171: 
172:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
173:     {
174:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
175:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
176:     }
177: 
178:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
179:     {
180:       if (!failed)
181:         {
182:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
183:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
184:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
185:         }
186:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
187:         {
188:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
189:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
190:            */
191: 
192:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
193:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
194:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
195:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
196:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
197:         }
198:       else
199:         {
200:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
201:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
202:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
203:             {
204:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
205:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
206:                */
207: 
208:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
209:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
210:             }
211:           else
212:             {
213:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
214:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
215:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
216:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
217:             }
218:         }
219: 
220:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
221:     }
222:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
223:     {
224:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
225:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
226:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
227:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
228:        */
229: 
230:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
231:     }
232: 
233:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
234:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
235: }

237: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
238:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
239: {
240:   uint8_t command = bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message);
241:   uint16_t length = message->payload_length;
242:   uint16_t first;
243:   bool failed = false;
244:   bool malformed = false;
245: 
246:   (void)arg;
247:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
248:     {
249:       return -EINVAL;
250:     }
251: 
252:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
253:     {
254:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
255:       failed = true;
256:       malformed = true;
257:     }
258:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)
259:     {
260:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
261:       failed = true;
262:       malformed = true;
263:     }
264:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
265:     {
266:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
267:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
268:       failed = true;
269:       malformed = true;
270:     }
271:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
272:     {
273:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
274:       failed = true;
275:       malformed = true;
276:     }
277: 
278:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
279:     {
280:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
281:         {
282:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
283:           failed = true;
284:           malformed = true;
285:         }
286:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
287:         {
288:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
289:           failed = true;
290:           malformed = true;
291:         }
292:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
293:         {
294:           failed = true;
295:         }
296:       else if (rx_free() < length)
297:         {
298:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
299:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
300:           failed = true;
301:         }
302:       else
303:         {
304:           const uint8_t *source =
305:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
306: 
307:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
308:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
309:           if (first > length)
310:             {
311:               first = length;
312:             }
313: 
314:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
315:           if (first != length)
316:             {
317:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
318:             }
319: 
320:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
321:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
322:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
323:         }
324:     }
325:   else if (!failed)
326:     {
327:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
328:         {
329:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
330:           failed = true;
331:           malformed = true;
332:         }
333:       else
334:         {
335:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
336:         }
337:     }
338: 
339:   if (!malformed)
340:     {
341:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
342: 
343:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
344:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
345:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
346:         {
347:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
348:         }
349:     }
350: 
351:   update_local_rts();
352:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
353:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
354:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
355: }

357: static int send_state_locked(void)
358: {
359:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
360:   int ret;
361: 
362:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
363:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_STATE, 0, 0, 0,
364:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
365:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
366:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
367:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
368:   if (ret == OK)
369:     {
370:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
371:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_STATE;
372:       g_uart.state_pending = false;
373:       g_uart.stats.state_tx++;
374:     }
375: 
376:   return ret;
377: }
378: 
379: static int send_data_locked(void)
380: {
381:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
382:   uint8_t *destination =
383:     (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
384:   uint16_t length = tx_count();
385:   uint16_t first;
386:   int ret;
387: 
388:   if (length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
389:     {
390:       length = BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE;
391:     }
392: 
393:   if (length == 0 || g_uart.peer_rts)
394:     {
395:       return -EAGAIN;
396:     }
397: 
398:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_read;
399:   if (first > length)
400:     {
401:       first = length;
402:     }
403: 
404:   memcpy(destination, &g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_read], first);
405:   if (first != length)
406:     {
407:       memcpy(destination + first, g_uart.tx_ring, length - first);
408:     }
409: 
410:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
411:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_DATA, 0, 0, 0,
412:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
413:   message.payload_address = BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
414:   message.payload_length = length;
415:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
416:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
417:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
418:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
419:   if (ret == OK)
420:     {
421:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
422:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_DATA;
423:       g_uart.tx_inflight = length;
424:       g_uart.stats.data_tx++;
425:     }
426: 
427:   return ret;
428: }

430: static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
431: {
432:   (void)argc;
433:   (void)argv;
434: 
435:   for (;;)
436:     {
437:       bk7258_mb_uart_callback_t callback;
438:       void *callback_arg;
439:       irqstate_t flags;
440:       enum bk7258_mb_link_state link;
441: 
442:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_uart.worker_sem,
443:                                            MB_UART_WORK_INTERVAL);
444:       nxsem_reset(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0);
445:       link = bk7258_mailbox_link_state();
446:       flags = up_irq_save();
447: 
448:       if (!g_uart.transaction_busy)
449:         {
450:           if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING && g_uart.state_pending)
451:             {
452:               (void)send_state_locked();
453:             }
454:           else if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
455:             {
456:               if (g_uart.state_pending)
457:                 {
458:                   (void)send_state_locked();
459:                 }
460:               else
461:                 {
462:                   (void)send_data_locked();
463:                 }
464:             }
465:         }
466: 
467:       callback = g_uart.callback;
468:       callback_arg = g_uart.callback_arg;
469:       up_irq_restore(flags);
470: 
471:       if (callback != NULL)
472:         {
473:           callback(callback_arg);
474:         }
475:     }
476: 
477:   return OK;
478: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_reset.c
3:  *
4:  * Chip reset for the AP core, i.e. what NSH's `reboot` needs.
5:  *
6:  * Why the AP needs its own reset path
7:  * ----------------------------------
8:  * Until this file existed the AP could not reset the board at all: NuttX had
9:  * no CONFIG_BOARDCTL_RESET here, so `reboot` was not even built, and every
10:  * reset in the development loop went through the CP shell's own `reboot`
11:  * instead (autoflash.sh and serial_cmd.sh both do that, because this board
12:  * has no auto-reset circuit on DTR/RTS -- see autoflash.sh's header).
13:  *
14:  * That CP path is slow, and measurably so.  Measured 2026-08-14, three runs,
15:  * identical to the millisecond: from the `reboot` echo on the CP console to
16:  * the CP's first boot line is 8.373s, of which the CP's own uptime counter
17:  * says only ~110ms is bootrom plus bootloader.  So the chip sits there for
18:  * 8.26s before it resets.  8000ms is CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS in the CP
19:  * build: the CP's `reboot` ends in bk_wdt_force_reboot(), which with
20:  * CONFIG_NMI_WDT_EN=1 takes wdt_hal_nmi_reboot() -- an NMI, not a reset --
21:  * and the NMI lands in the two-core dump/handover machinery in
22:  * cp/middleware/arch/cm33/trap_base.c, which our NuttX AP does not
23:  * participate in.  Nothing resets the part until the interrupt watchdog
24:  * expires.
25:  *
26:  * The AON watchdog does not have that problem.  It is the same register the
27:  * CP uses in its *non*-NMI branch (wdt_hal_force_reboot(), the #else side):
28:  * write the period with the two-stage key and the part resets, with no NMI,
29:  * no dump handover and nobody to wait for.
30:  *
31:  * Register: AON_WDT_R_CTRL at 0x44000600, one word --
32:  *   bits [15:0]  period
33:  *   bits [23:16] key: write 0x5A then 0xA5 to commit
34:  * (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/aon_wdt_reg.h; the sequence and the
35:  * period value 0x0A are taken verbatim from wdt_hal_force_reboot() in
36:  * ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/wdt_hal.c.)
37:  *
38:  * The register map is shared and flat -- the AP build defines
39:  * SOC_ADDR_OFFSET as 0, and this driver already drives AON GPIO at
40:  * 0x44000400 -- so the AP can reach the AON watchdog directly and does not
41:  * need the CP's cooperation.  Asking the CP over the mailbox would not help
42:  * anyway: its IPC_CPU1_NEED_REBOOT handler calls the same
43:  * bk_wdt_force_reboot() that takes 8s (cp mb_ipc_cmd.c).
44:  *
45:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
46:  ****************************************************************************/
47:

49:  * Included Files
50:  ****************************************************************************/

59: #include "arm_internal.h"
60: 
61: /****************************************************************************
62:  * Pre-processor Definitions
63:  ****************************************************************************/
64: 
65: #define BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL     0x44000600u
66: 
67: #define BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_1ST  0x5au
68: #define BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_2ND  0xa5u
69: #define BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_S    16
70: 
71: /* Smallest period the vendor itself uses for a forced reboot.  The AON
72:  * watchdog counts on the always-on 32kHz domain, so ten ticks is a fraction
73:  * of a millisecond -- the reset is effectively immediate.
74:  */
75: 
76: #define BK7258_AON_WDT_PERIOD   0x000au
77: 
78: /****************************************************************************
79:  * Public Functions
80:  ****************************************************************************/
81: 
82: /****************************************************************************
83:  * Name: board_reset
84:  *
85:  * Description:
86:  *   Reset the whole chip.  Invoked by BOARDIOC_RESET, which is what NSH's
87:  *   `reboot` command issues.  status is the caller's reset reason; this part
88:  *   has nowhere to record it that survives an AON watchdog reset, so it is
89:  *   accepted and ignored rather than pretended about.
90:  *
91:  *   Does not return.
92:  *
93:  ****************************************************************************/
94: 
95: int board_reset(int status)
96: {
97:   UNUSED(status);
98: 
99:   /* Interrupts off first: once the period is committed the part is going
100:    * down within a fraction of a millisecond, and there is no useful work
101:    * left to do.  Leaving them on would only widen the window in which an
102:    * ISR runs against half-torn-down state.
103:    */
104: 
105:   up_irq_save();
106: 
107:   putreg32((BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_1ST << BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_S) |
108:            BK7258_AON_WDT_PERIOD, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
109:   putreg32((BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_2ND << BK7258_AON_WDT_KEY_S) |
110:            BK7258_AON_WDT_PERIOD, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
111: 
112:   for (; ; )
113:     {
114:       /* The watchdog does the rest.  If it somehow does not, hanging here is
115:        * the honest outcome: returning would let the caller report a reset
116:        * that never happened.
117:        */
118:     }
119: 
120:   return 0;
121: }

210: static void ap_bridge_task(beken_thread_arg_t arg)
211: {
212: 	u8 input[MB_CHNL_BUFF_LEN];
213: 	u8 line[AP_BRIDGE_LOG_LINE_SIZE];
214: 	u16 line_length = 0;
215: 	u8 active_mode = AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_LOG;
216: 	bool line_continues = false;
217: 
218: 	(void)arg;
219: 	for (;;)
220: 	{
221: 		u32 events;
222: 		u32 flags;
223: 		u16 input_length;
224: 		u16 index;
225: 		u8 ready_set;
226: 		u8 ready_clear;
227: 		u8 ready_before;
228: 		bk_err_t ret = rtos_get_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.sem,
229: 			line_length ? AP_BRIDGE_LOG_FLUSH_MS : 20);
230: 
231: 		bk_mb_uart_poll(MB_UART0);
232: 
233: 		flags = rtos_disable_int();
234: 		events = s_ap_bridge.events;
235: 		s_ap_bridge.events = 0;
236: 		ready_set = s_ap_bridge.ready_set;
237: 		ready_clear = s_ap_bridge.ready_clear;
238: 		ready_before = s_ap_bridge.ready_flags;
239: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_set = 0;
240: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_clear = 0;
241: 		rtos_enable_int(flags);
242: 
243: 		if (events & (AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_DOWN | AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET |
244: 			      AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT))
245: 		{
246: 			ready_clear |= AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
247: 		}
248: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_flags |= ready_set;
249: 		s_ap_bridge.ready_flags &= ~ready_clear;
250: 		/* poll() may complete recovery in the same iteration that consumes an
251: 		 * older timeout/reset event.  The driver's current state is the final
252: 		 * authority for the MBUART gate, so a stale event cannot clear a newer
253: 		 * READY notification permanently.
254: 		 */
255: 		if (bk_mb_uart_is_link_ready(MB_UART0))
256: 			s_ap_bridge.ready_flags |= AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
257: 		else
258: 			s_ap_bridge.ready_flags &= ~AP_BRIDGE_READY_MBUART;
259: 		s_ap_bridge.link_ready =
260: 			(s_ap_bridge.ready_flags & AP_BRIDGE_READY_ALL) ==
261: 			AP_BRIDGE_READY_ALL && bk_mb_uart_is_link_ready(MB_UART0);
262: 
263: 		if (s_ap_bridge.mode_applied_generation !=
264: 			s_ap_bridge.mode_generation)
265: 		{
266: 			if (line_length)
267: 				ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length, !line_continues);
268: 			line_length = 0;
269: 			line_continues = false;
270: 			active_mode = s_ap_bridge.requested_mode;
271: 			s_ap_bridge.output_mode = active_mode;
272: 			s_ap_bridge.mode_applied_generation =
273: 				s_ap_bridge.mode_generation;
274: 			rtos_set_semaphore(&s_ap_bridge.mode_sem);
275: 		}
276: 
277: 		do
278: 		{
279: 			input_length = bk_mb_uart_read(MB_UART0, input, sizeof(input));
280: 			s_ap_bridge.stats.rx_bytes += input_length;
281: 			if (active_mode == AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_RAW)
282: 			{
283: 				if (input_length && !shell_log_raw_data_nonblock(input, input_length))
284: 					s_ap_bridge.stats.rx_queue_fail++;
285: 				continue;
286: 			}
287: 
288: 			for (index = 0; index < input_length; index++)
289: 			{
290: 				line[line_length++] = input[index];
291: 				if (input[index] == '\n' || line_length == sizeof(line))
292: 				{
293: 					bool complete = input[index] == '\n';
294: 
295: 					ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length,
296: 							     !line_continues);
297: 					line_length = 0;
298: 					line_continues = !complete;
299: 				}
300: 			}
301: 		} while (input_length != 0);
302: 
303: 		if (ret == kTimeoutErr && line_length &&
304: 			active_mode == AP_CONSOLE_OUTPUT_LOG)
305: 		{
306: 			ap_bridge_log_output(line, line_length, !line_continues);
307: 			line_length = 0;
308: 			line_continues = true;
309: 		}
310: 
311: 		ap_bridge_drain_tx();
312: 
313: 		if (events & (AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_DOWN | AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET |
314: 			      AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT))
315: 		{
316: 			u32 now = rtos_get_time();
317: 
318: 			s_ap_bridge.stats.link_down++;
319: 			if (events & AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_RESET)
320: 				s_ap_bridge.stats.reset++;
321: 			if (events & AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TIMEOUT)
322: 				s_ap_bridge.stats.timeout++;
323: 			if ((ready_before & (AP_BRIDGE_READY_IPC |
324: 					     AP_BRIDGE_READY_PWC)) ==
325: 				(AP_BRIDGE_READY_IPC | AP_BRIDGE_READY_PWC) &&
326: 				(u32)(now - s_ap_bridge.last_down_log_ms) >= 1000)
327: 			{
328: 				s_ap_bridge.last_down_log_ms = now;
329: 				BK_LOGW(AP_BRIDGE_TAG,
330: 					"link down event=%x queued=%u ready=%x\r\n",
331: 					events, ap_bridge_tx_count(),
332: 					s_ap_bridge.ready_flags);
333: 			}
334: 			if (!s_ap_bridge.link_ready)
335: 				shell_ap_console_link_down();
336: 		}
337: 	}
338: }

405: u16 ap_console_bridge_write(const u8 *data, u16 length)
406: {
407: 	u16 written = 0;
408: 
409: 	if (!data || !length || !s_ap_bridge.link_ready)
410: 		return 0;
411: 
412: 	rtos_lock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
413: 	while (written < length)
414: 	{
415: 		u16 next = (s_ap_bridge.tx_wr + 1) % sizeof(s_ap_bridge.tx_ring);
416: 		if (next == s_ap_bridge.tx_rd)
417: 			break;
418: 		s_ap_bridge.tx_ring[s_ap_bridge.tx_wr] = data[written++];
419: 		s_ap_bridge.tx_wr = next;
420: 	}
421: 	rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_ap_bridge.tx_mutex);
422: 	if (written < length)
423: 	{
424: 		s_ap_bridge.stats.tx_drop += length - written;
425: 	}
426: 	if (written)
427: 		ap_bridge_wake(AP_BRIDGE_EVENT_TX);
428: 	return written;
429: }

text:
结论：**不能据此认定是 UI/LCD 卡顿导致的，但它暴露了自动烧录脚本中的控制台切换竞态。负载升高可能让这个竞态更容易出现。**

**日志证据**
失败发生在烧录开始前：

```text
Getting Bus...
LinkCheck Timeout
GetBus fail!
```

说明：

- 镜像没有开始擦除或写入。
- `bk_loader` 没等到芯片复位后的 BootROM。
- 问题是软复位命令没有成功触发整机复位，不是 Flash 传输卡顿。

而且该问题不是当前版本才出现。现有日志中，8 月 18 至 20 日也有多次相同的 `LinkCheck Timeout`。同一天还出现了：

```text
10:12:13 失败
10:12:46 成功
10:16:13 失败
```

这更符合间歇性时序竞态，而不是固件稳定卡死。

**具体竞态**
旧脚本执行：

```text
Ctrl-]
.
等待 50 ms
换行
reboot
```

CP 收到 `Ctrl-] .` 后并不会同步切回 CP shell，只会设置 `SHELL_EVENT_AP_SWITCH`。CP shell 主循环的处理顺序是：

```c
if (Events & SHELL_EVENT_RX_IND)
  rx_ind_process();

if (Events & SHELL_EVENT_AP_SWITCH)
  shell_ap_console_switch_process();
```

因此如果 `reboot` 到达过快，同一轮中会先处理 RX，再执行 owner 切换。结果可能是：

- `reboot` 仍被转发给 AP；
- owner 处于 pending 时，`reboot` 被丢弃；
- 命令与转义残留拼接，无法识别。

原先固定的 `50 ms` 只是概率性规避。系统负载或 bridge 调度变化后，50 ms 不再可靠。

**与屏幕卡顿的关系**
物理 UART 和退出转义由 CP 核处理，VelaSight/LVGL 在 AP 核运行。因此正常的同步 LCD 刷新不会直接阻止 CP 接收串口。

可能存在的间接关系是：

```text
AP负载增加
-> mailbox bridge响应变慢
-> AP/CP控制台切换窗口变长
-> 旧脚本50 ms等待更容易撞上竞态
```

所以它可能和高负载相关，但不是“LCD 一卡，CP 就无法复位”的直接证明。

**已修复脚本**
已修改 `autoflash.sh`：

1. 优先向当前 shell 直接发送 `reboot`。
2. AP 当前已经实现 AON watchdog 整机复位，不需要必须退出到 CP。
3. 如果直接复位失败，再执行 `Ctrl-] .` 回退到 CP。
4. CP owner 切换等待由 `50 ms` 增至 `300 ms`。
5. 保留轮询 `Gotten Bus`，拿到总线后立即停止写串口。

新的关键流程：

```text
当前 shell 直接 reboot
-> 等待 BootROM
-> 若失败，Ctrl-] .
-> 等待 300 ms
-> CP shell reboot
```

`bash -n ./autoflash.sh` 和 `git diff --check` 均已通过。

可以用只测试握手、不写 Flash的方式连续验证：

```bash
./autoflash.sh -t -b 1500000 -B 115200 -p /dev/ttyUSB0
```

建议连续运行 10 次。如果新脚本仍频繁失败，再分别测试：

```text
停留在 CP `$` 提示符时测试
进入 AP `nsh>` 后测试
屏幕静止时测试
长按动画期间测试
```

只有当“长按动画期间失败率显著高于 CP shell/静止状态”时，才能进一步把它和 AP mailbox 或 LCD 高负载联系起来。脚本修复当前尚未提交。

440:   if (display == NULL || snapshot == NULL)

443:   /* fb1 is the physical left content display; fb0 is the physical right
444:    * status display. */
445:   content_dirty = !display->previous_valid ||
446:                   vs_content_changed(snapshot, &display->previous);
447:   status_dirty = !display->previous_valid ||
448:                  vs_status_changed(snapshot, &display->previous);

456:       /* Match the old synchronous boot animation's hand-off: both complete
457:        * frames must reach panel GRAM before the shared backlight is enabled.
458:        * lv_refr_now() executes each framebuffer's FBIO_UPDATE synchronously. */

460:       lv_obj_invalidate(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].screen);
461:       lv_obj_invalidate(display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL].screen);
462:       lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].display);

470:     {
471:       /* State changes normally wait for LVGL's 33 ms refresh timer.  That
472:        * timer is too coarse for button feedback, and a full-frame LCD push
473:        * can make the next timer pass arrive even later.  Flush only the
474:        * panels changed by this snapshot now; the regular timer remains
475:        * responsible for its own animations such as the waiting suffix. */
476:       if (status_dirty)
477:         lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_STATUS_PANEL].display);
478:       if (content_dirty)
479:         lv_refr_now(display->panel[VS_CONTENT_PANEL].display);

482:   display->previous_valid = true;
483:   display->waiting = snapshot->progress_kind == VS_PROGRESS_WAIT;
484:   snprintf(display->wait_meta, sizeof(display->wait_meta), "%s",
485:            snapshot->status_meta);
486:   if (!display->waiting)

488:       display->wait_phase = 0;
489:       display->wait_next_ms = 0;

73: int vs_input_poll(struct vs_input_s *input, struct vs_input_event_s *event)
74: {
75:   uint32_t now;
76:   uint32_t buttons;
77:   int key;
78: 
79:   if (input == NULL || event == NULL)
80:     {
81:       return -EINVAL;
82:     }
83: 
84:   memset(event, 0, sizeof(*event));
85:   event->type = VS_INPUT_NONE;
86:   now = vs_input_now_ms();
87:   buttons = board_buttons();
88: 
89:   for (key = 0; key < VS_KEY_COUNT; key++)
90:     {
91:       struct vs_key_state_s *state = &input->key[key];
92:       bool raw = (buttons & vs_input_mask(key)) != 0;
93: 
94:       if (raw != state->raw)
95:         {
96:           state->raw = raw;
97:           state->samples = 1;
98:         }
99:       else if (state->samples < VS_INPUT_DEBOUNCE_SAMPLES)
100:         {
101:           state->samples++;
102:         }
103: 
104:       if (state->samples == VS_INPUT_DEBOUNCE_SAMPLES &&
105:           state->stable != state->raw)
106:         {
107:           state->stable = state->raw;
108:           if (state->stable)
109:             {
110:               state->pressed_ms = now;
111:               state->long_sent = false;
112:               state->last_progress = 0xff;
113:               event->type = VS_INPUT_PRESS;
114:               event->key = key;
115:               event->held_ms = 0;
116:               return 1;
117:             }
118:           else if (!state->long_sent && !input->combo_sent &&
119:                    !input->combo_started &&
120:                    now - state->pressed_ms >= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MIN_MS &&
121:                    now - state->pressed_ms <= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS)
122:             {
123:               event->type = VS_INPUT_SHORT;
124:               event->key = key;
125:               event->held_ms = now - state->pressed_ms;
126:               return 1;
127:             }
128:           else if (!state->long_sent && !input->combo_sent &&
129:                    !input->combo_started &&
130:                    now - state->pressed_ms > CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS)
131:             {
132:               state->long_sent = true;
133:               event->type = VS_INPUT_CANCEL;
134:               event->key = key;
135:               event->held_ms = now - state->pressed_ms;
136:               return 1;
137:             }
138:         }
139:     }
140: 
141:   if (input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].stable && input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].stable)
142:     {
143:       uint32_t start = input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].pressed_ms;
144:       uint32_t held;
145:       uint8_t progress;
146: 
147:       if (input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].pressed_ms > start)
148:         {
149:           start = input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].pressed_ms;
150:         }
151: 
152:       if (!input->combo_started)
153:         {
154:           input->combo_started = true;
155:           input->combo_start_ms = start;
156:           input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].last_progress = 0xff;
157:           event->type = VS_INPUT_COMBO_PROGRESS;
158:           event->key = VS_KEY_BACK;
159:           event->progress = 0;
160:           event->held_ms = 0;
161:           return 1;
162:         }
163: 
164:       held = now - start;
165:       progress = (uint8_t)(held * 100u / CONFIG_VS_COMBO_PRESS_MS);
166:       if (progress > 100)
167:         {
168:           progress = 100;
169:         }
170: 
171:       if (!input->combo_sent && progress < 100 &&
172:           progress / 2u * 2u != input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].last_progress)
173:         {
174:           input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].last_progress = progress / 2u * 2u;
175:           event->type = VS_INPUT_COMBO_PROGRESS;
176:           event->key = VS_KEY_BACK;
177:           event->progress = input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].last_progress;
178:           event->held_ms = held;
179:           return 1;
180:         }
181: 
182:       if (!input->combo_sent && held >= CONFIG_VS_COMBO_PRESS_MS)
183:         {
184:           input->combo_sent = true;
185:           input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].long_sent = true;
186:           input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].long_sent = true;
187:           event->type = VS_INPUT_NET_TOGGLE;
188:           event->held_ms = held;
189:           return 1;
190:         }
191:     }
192:   else if (input->combo_started && !input->combo_sent)
193:     {
194:       uint32_t held = now - input->combo_start_ms;
195: 
196:       input->combo_sent = true;
197:       input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].long_sent = true;
198:       input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].long_sent = true;
199:       if (held >= CONFIG_VS_COMBO_PRESS_MS)
200:         {
201:           event->type = VS_INPUT_NET_TOGGLE;
202:           event->held_ms = held;
203:           return 1;
204:         }
205: 
206:       event->type = VS_INPUT_COMBO_CANCEL;
207:       event->held_ms = held;
208:       return 1;
209:     }
210:   else if (!input->key[VS_KEY_BACK].stable &&
211:            !input->key[VS_KEY_NEXT].stable)
212:     {
213:       input->combo_sent = false;
214:       input->combo_started = false;
215:     }
216: 
217:   for (key = 0; key < VS_KEY_COUNT; key++)
218:     {
219:       struct vs_key_state_s *state = &input->key[key];
220:       uint32_t held;
221: 
222:       if (!state->stable || state->long_sent || input->combo_sent ||
223:           input->combo_started)
224:         {
225:           continue;
226:         }
227: 
228:       held = now - state->pressed_ms;
229:       if (held >= CONFIG_VS_LONG_PRESS_MS)
230:         {
231:           state->long_sent = true;
232:           event->type = VS_INPUT_LONG;
233:           event->key = key;
234:           event->progress = 100;
235:           event->held_ms = held;
236:           return 1;
237:         }
238: 
239:       if (key == VS_KEY_CONFIRM || key == VS_KEY_BACK)
240:         {
241:           uint32_t progress_ms;
242:           uint32_t progress_range;
243:           uint8_t progress;
244: 
245:           if (held <= CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS)
246:             {
247:               continue;
248:             }
249: 
250:           progress_ms = held - CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS;
251:           progress_range = CONFIG_VS_LONG_PRESS_MS >
252:                            CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS ?
253:                            CONFIG_VS_LONG_PRESS_MS -
254:                            CONFIG_VS_SHORT_PRESS_MAX_MS : 1;
255:           progress = (uint8_t)(progress_ms * 100u / progress_range);
256: 
257:           progress = (uint8_t)(progress / 2u * 2u);
258:           if (progress != state->last_progress)
259:             {
260:               state->last_progress = progress;
261:               event->type = VS_INPUT_PROGRESS;
262:               event->key = key;
263:               event->progress = progress;
264:               event->held_ms = held;
265:               return 1;
266:             }
267:         }
268:     }
269: 
270:   return 0;
271: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_gc9d01_fb.c
3:  *
4:  * openvela framebuffer driver for the GC9D01 panels (160x160 round, RGB565,
5:  * one per QSPI controller).  Implements the three hooks fb_register() needs
6:  * -- up_fbinitialize(), up_fbgetvplane(), up_fbuninitialize() -- plus the
7:  * fb_vtable_s entries required for a panel that has no autonomous refresh:
8:  * getvideoinfo, getplaneinfo and updatearea.
9:  *
10:  * Why updatearea is mandatory here: a RAM-less RGB parallel panel is
11:  * scanned out continuously by an LCD controller, so writing the
12:  * framebuffer is enough.  GC9D01 has its own GRAM and is written over a
13:  * serial bus, so nothing reaches the glass until the driver explicitly
14:  * pushes it.  Without CONFIG_FB_UPDATE + this callback the screen would
15:  * simply never change.
16:  *
17:  * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
18:  * Multiple displays
19:  * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
20:  * fb_register(display, plane) (include/nuttx/video/fb.h) calls
21:  * up_fbinitialize(display), then up_fbgetvplane(display, plane), then
22:  * fb_register_device(), which names the node /dev/fb<display>.  So exposing
23:  * two panels is just a matter of calling fb_register() twice.
24:  *
25:  * The constraint that shapes this file: fb_vtable_s's callbacks receive
26:  * only the vtable pointer, with no display argument.  A single shared
27:  * vtable therefore cannot tell which panel it is being asked about.  Each
28:  * display consequently gets its own state structure whose *first* member is
29:  * the vtable, so a callback can recover its own state by casting the vtable
30:  * pointer back (the usual container-of trick, valid here because the vtable
31:  * sits at offset 0).
32:  *

196: static int gc9d01_push(FAR struct gc9d01_fb_s *priv)
197: {
198:   clock_t start = clock_systime_ticks();
199: 
200:   if (priv->fbmem == NULL || priv->bus < 0)
201:     {
202:       return -ENODEV;
203:     }
204: 
205:   if (!bk7258_gc9d01_window_full(priv->display))
206:     {
207:       return -EIO;
208:     }
209: 
210:   if (!bk7258_lcd_spi_write_frame(priv->bus, priv->fbmem, GC9D01_FBLEN))
211:     {
212:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: pixel burst failed\n", priv->display);
213:       return -EIO;
214:     }
215: 
216:   priv->updates++;
217: 
218:   {
219:     uint32_t ms = TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - start);
220: 
221:     priv->report_updates++;
222:     priv->report_ms += ms;
223:     if (ms > priv->report_max_ms)
224:       {
225:         priv->report_max_ms = ms;
226:       }
227: 
228:     /* Report a rolling bus cost without logging every frame.  This makes it
229:      * possible to distinguish LVGL scheduling delay from LCD transfer time
230:      * during a long-press test. */
231:     if ((priv->updates % 32u) == 0)
232:       {
233:         printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: 32 updates avg=%ums max=%ums total=%u\n",
234:                priv->display,
235:                (unsigned int)(priv->report_ms / priv->report_updates),
236:                (unsigned int)priv->report_max_ms,
237:                (unsigned int)priv->updates);
238:         priv->report_updates = 0;
239:         priv->report_ms = 0;
240:         priv->report_max_ms = 0;
241:       }
242:   }
243: 
244:   /* First few pushes get a timing report: it is the only way to know the
245:    * real cost of a frame on this bus, which decides whether the preview
246:    * path needs DMA.  After that stay quiet -- this runs per displayed
247:    * frame.
248:    */
249: 
250:   if (priv->updates <= 3)
251:     {
252:       uint32_t ms = TICK2MSEC(clock_systime_ticks() - start);
253: 
254:       printf("gc9d01_fb[%d]: update %u: %d bytes in %ums "
255:              "(%u frames on bus)\n", priv->display,
256:              (unsigned int)priv->updates, GC9D01_FBLEN, (unsigned int)ms,
257:              (unsigned int)bk7258_lcd_spi_frame_count(priv->bus));
258:     }
259: 
260:   return OK;
261: }
